# Gradient Boosting and Stacking

**Estimated time: 1.5 hours**

Continue reading **Chapter 7: Ensemble Learning and Random Forests**, starting with the **Boosting** section and continuing to the end of the chapter.

In the course edition, this corresponds approximately to **pp. 222–235**.

The main focus is gradient boosting: building trees sequentially so that each new model attempts to correct errors made by the models that came before it.

The chapter also introduces **stacking**. You do not need to master stacking at this stage, but you should understand the basic idea and recognize it as another ensemble-learning strategy.

## First Pass: Get the Big Picture — 10 minutes

- Skim the remaining section titles.
- Look at the plots and figures.
- Read exercise questions 6–7.

## Second Pass: Read for Understanding — 60 minutes

Read the remainder of the chapter carefully.

Focus especially on:

- the general idea of boosting;
- how sequential learning differs from the independent trees used in a random forest;
- how gradient boosting improves a model iteratively;
- the basic idea behind stacking.

## Third Pass: Review — 20 minutes

Answer exercise questions 6–7.

Return to the relevant sections when needed and make sure you can explain the main ideas in your own words.
